findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT - Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a trash can was obstructing easy access to the handwashing sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the trash can was moved to a different location. Ensure the handwashing sink is easily accessible at all times for employees.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [PF]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed the quaternary ammonium sanitizer on the dough prep table was testing at 50 ppm. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the sanitizer was remade to achieve a concentration level of 200 ppm. Ensure the sanitizer concentration level is maintained between 200 - 400 ppm at all times.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following time/temperature for safety (TCS) foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” stored on a dry storage shelf in the kitchen:

- “Barbecue sauce in refill bottles.”
- “Grated Parmesan cheese.”

CORRECTED - PIC was informed, and the foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are stored under refrigeration and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less after opening.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspectors observed the shelves holding clean dishes across from the triple sink to be soiled with debris. 

Inspectors also observed the shelf across the serving area holding disposable plates to have accumulation of grease deposits.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned regularly to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed an employee working does not have food handler training certificate. PIC was informed to ensure all employees who do not have a CFPM certificate must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all employees obtain a food handlers certificate by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed no one present at the facility has a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificate. The PIC was reminded that there must be a CFPM present during all hours of operation. Ensure that there is a CFPM present at the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the hand washing sink adjacent to the triple sink did not have paper towels when the inspector arrived. The PIC re-filled the paper towels dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that hand washing sinks always has paper towels available for the proper hand washing procedure.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. The inspector educated that sanitizer buckets must always be available to sanitize food contact surfaces and store wet wiping cloths. An employee made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the shelves holding clean dishes across from the triple sink are soiled with debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves across from the triple sink are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed wet mops stored with the heads in the mop sink basin. The PIC was informed and they inverted the mops during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
Observed that no one at the facility could show the inspector their CFPM certificate. The PIC stated that their CFPM certification had recently expired, and the other employee working stated that they had taken the class and passed the exam, but they did not have a copy of their certificate or any proof that they took the class. The PIC said they will work on getting more CFPM’s at the facility. Ensure there is always a CFPM at the facility during all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the shelves holding foods, single service, and clean dishes are soiled with debris. The locations of these shelves include to the right of the prep cooler and across the dish area. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ceiling tiles in the bathroom have not been changed to vinyl coated. The PIC has purchased the vinyl tiles and they are at the facility, but they have not been installed yet. Ensure that materials are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and nonabsorbent

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a mop being stored with the head in the mop bucket water. The mop head was moved out of the water during the inspection.  Mops always need to be placed in a position that allows the head to air dry when not in use. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.
